reason: The immature red cells appear to be making proteins, and the supplied materials should let them make haemoglobin for carrying oxygen.
expectation: The cells will make haemoglobin as they develop.

effect: The developing cells made haemoglobin and matured into red blood cells, so they appear ready to interact with oxygen.
reaction: The cutaway makes the change from developing cells to mature discs clear.
reason: Haemoglobin in red blood cells carries oxygen, so these are a plausible pair.
expectation: The red blood cells will pick up oxygen.

effect: The red cells now carry oxygen, and the double arrow shows that haemoglobin can also release it in tissues.
reaction: The connection between oxygen release and working tissues is useful.
reason: Plasma solutes dissolved in plasma water should form the liquid part of the blood sample.
expectation: This will make plasma for the blood sample.

effect: The water and solutes formed plasma, providing the liquid part of the sample.
reason: The oxygen-bearing red cells should be suspended in plasma to help form the blood sample.
expectation: The red cells will join the plasma.

effect: Plasma had to be combined with white cells and platelets first; the oxygen-bearing red cells remain to be added.
reaction: The required order surprised me, though the compatibility feedback made the next step clear.
reason: Adding the oxygen-bearing red cells should complete the blood sample.

choice.combine: Plasma with white cells and platelets

expectation: The red cells will join the plasma, white cells and platelets to make a blood sample.

effect: Adding the oxygen-bearing red cells completed the blood sample and clarified that plasma and red cells carry different materials.
reaction: The finished sample brought the separate components together clearly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding oxygen to the red cells was most worthwhile: the result explained both binding and release, connecting the carrier to working tissues.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making plasma was straightforward but offered less explanation of what its solutes contribute.

surprise.text: I expected to add red cells to plasma immediately, but the game required white cells and platelets first.

arbitrary.text: The required order for adding blood cells felt arbitrary because the result did not explain why red cells could not be added first. The compatibility feedback did make progress clear.

continue.text: I would choose to continue to see how circulation brings oxygen to tissues. The explanation of oxygen release made that connection interesting, though the sample assembly itself was mostly predictable.
